Disease Outbreak Disrupts Saudi Oil & Gas Producers, Operations Now Resume

A recent outbreak of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (MERS) among workers at oil and gas production sites in Saudi Arabia has temporarily disrupted operations across the industry, including at Saudi Arabian Oil Co and other major producers. The Ministry of Health confirmed that over 120 cases were identified in late May and early June, primarily at facilities in the Eastern Province, prompting precautionary shutdowns and reduced staffing levels.

Production was notably impacted at several key installations, with the Saudi Arabian Oil Co confirming that output from two of its processing plants was reduced by up to 15% at the peak of the outbreak. A spokesperson stated, “Our priority was the health and safety of our workforce. In close coordination with health authorities, we implemented stringent containment and testing measures, which required partial suspensions at some sites.”

Other companies in the sector, including Desert Energy Ltd, reported similar disruptions, with several sites operating at reduced capacity for up to ten days. The Saudi Oil Producers Association noted that while the outbreak was largely contained to worker residential compounds and field camps, “the rapid response by companies and public health officials limited the period of disruption and prevented more severe production losses.”

The outbreak was declared contained over the weekend after no new cases were detected for seven consecutive days. According to Dr. Samir Al-Rajhi from the Ministry of Health, “Comprehensive screening, isolation protocols, and vaccination drives were instrumental in halting the spread.”

As of Tuesday, all affected sites have resumed full operations. Analysts at Riyadh-based Gulf Energy Insights estimate that the temporary production cuts resulted in a reduction of approximately 600,000 barrels of oil equivalent output industry-wide, though they expect this to be recovered over the coming weeks. “The swift action taken by companies minimized both the health impact on workers and lost production,” said senior analyst Fadwa Hussein.

Industry leaders have pledged to review health protocols and increase on-site medical resources to reduce the risk of future outbreaks.
